rule: A dead node-type/field literal is registered BY NAME with an owner and a reason. A literal the record does not name fails. A recorded entry with no reason fails. A recorded literal that disappears fails too: the record is a decision, so a repayment is written down here in the same round that removes it.

2026-09-26 — bash fully repaid (1 -> 0). The single registered dead literal `identifier` (real-bash-analyzer.ts:299, a `.type === "identifier"` alternative in the function-name reader) is DELETED, not retyped: the pinned grammar has no `identifier` node, and the surviving `word` branch already covers the position, so there was nothing to add. The same rewrite ADDED six node types to the analyzer (arithmetic_expansion, postfix_expression, c_style_for_statement, ERROR, plus the three the traversal now consults), so refs 26 -> 32. One of the six — `arithmetic_expression` — was a plausible guess at a fourth arithmetic node shape; this same gate reported it as a dead branch on the day it was written, and it was removed in the same round rather than registered as tolerated debt. That is the gate refusing a guess, which is the only reason the guess did not become a permanent record. bash F1: PASS, refs=32, unknown=0, unknownFields=0. css: 4 -> 0, all four repaid 2026-09-26 against the PINNED wasm's own 151-type enumeration (script/m14/tmp/css-grammar-repayment.ts), not by reading the analyzer. `mixin_statement` and `include_statement` were REDUNDANT, not load-bearing: the CSS grammar has no SCSS productions, so `@mixin card {}` and `.a { @include card; }` arrive as `at_rule` with an `at_keyword` child, and the `at_rule` case already handled both (verified live: the mixin symbol, the @include symbol and the `uses .a -> "@mixin card"` edge all resolve). `variable_name` does not exist and never did. `media_query_list` did not exist either, and removing it REVEALED a defect rather than causing one: the union was missing `unary_query` and `selector_query`, so `@media not print` and `@media selector(.a)` lost their scope entirely — no contains edge, and the Responsive-Design pattern unset. Both are now in the union. Two further DEAD VALUE-POSITION branches were removed in the same round, a class the type-literal audit cannot see: `propName.startsWith("$")` (SCSS) and `startsWith("@")` (LESS). Measured, `$x: 1` and `@x: 1` each yield ERROR nodes and ZERO property_name nodes at top level and inside a rule, so no such text can reach the predicate — meaning the LESS framework signal was never emitted by anything, and SCSS/SASS is in fact detected from the at_rule path instead. WAVE 1a (the three redundant/dead removals) is PROVEN BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING: the corpus output over 457 files across 13 corpora is byte-identical, digest a537541b0136297960deb31e4f16d908a729139b93ac2704bb24da16b0446030 before and after (script/m14/tmp/css-edge-digest.ts). WAVE 1b (media_query_list) is NOT behaviour-preserving and is justified by PROBE + FIXTURE, not by a corpus delta: the corpus digest is UNCHANGED by it, which means no file in the 457-file corpus contains `@media not` or `@media selector(…)` at all. Stated plainly rather than dressed as a corpus win.

REPAYMENT RECORDED 2026-09-27 (markdown, M14 #290 — the lane's F1 cell was red for the whole life of this record). markdown's two entries are removed, and the repayment is the OPPOSITE of every repayment above: the literals stayed and the ORACLE was fixed.

Both entries were `uri_autolink` and `email_autolink` at real-markdown-analyzer.ts:253, and the record's own reason named the two possible repayments: "either load tree-sitter-markdown_inline into the oracle for this lane (EXTRA_GRAMMARS) or delete the branch." The second was the dangerous one. tree-sitter-markdown ships as a BLOCK grammar plus a COMPANION INLINE grammar, and the engine pre-parses every `inline` node with the companion before handing the trees to the analyzer (the vue/svelte SFC pattern), so the analyzer was reading node types the single-grammar oracle could not see. Both are live NAMED types of the pinned inline grammar — ids 37 and 38, measured against the shipped bytes, not inferred. So the entries were not dead branches; they were a live branch reported dead by a gate that was only half the oracle.

A gate that reports a live branch as dead is worse than a gate that reports nothing, because the natural response to its output is to DELETE the branch — and deleting it would have silently removed every autolink edge markdown emits, turning a measurable gap into an unmeasurable one. The lane had been carrying a `markdown FAIL unknown=2` row in M14.0.F1 for 35 days, and the standing instruction in this repo is that a red grammar cell must be closed, not baselined deeper. The correct move was to make the cell mean what it says.

The fix is one line: `markdown: ["tree-sitter-markdown_inline.wasm"]` in EXTRA_GRAMMARS at script/m14/audit-analyzer-grammar.ts, alongside the vue/svelte/typescript/html entries that already did exactly this for their own companion grammars. markdown now audits refs=4 unknown=0 unknownFields=0, and the `lang-completion-matrix` grammar column reads PASS. Re-introducing either spelling as an UNKNOWN would require DELETING the line above, which is now the thing that would need its own written-down decision.

What this did NOT buy, and is not claimed: the entries were the cheapest defect in the lane. The two UNPINNED grammars behind this one (the inline wasm carried no sha256 in validation/m14/grammar-pins.json, which covers ten lanes and not this one) are a larger hole, and the inline grammar being absent from the oracle is the same fact seen from the other side: this lane's grammar was only ever half-pinned, and half-oracled.
